title: Choose the highest useful API.

# Codex PPT Slide Image Prompt

## Canvas
{
  "type": "16:9 full-slide PowerPoint image",
  "language": "English",
  "slide_number": 8,
  "render_slide_number": false
}

## Required Background
{
  "deck_context": {
    "source_summary": "Class 16 begins Week 4 of a traditional AEM Sites course for frontend-oriented developers. It builds the minimum Java runtime vocabulary needed before Sling Models: core module, OSGi bundle, Declarative Services component, service contract, runtime states and Sling Resource API.",
    "core_claim": "Compiled Java becomes an AEM capability only after bundle packaging and resolution, Declarative Services lifecycle requirements and a correct content boundary; diagnose each handoff with observable runtime evidence.",
    "canonical_facts": [
      "The Maven core module produces the project's OSGi bundle JAR.",
      "A bundle manifest declares symbolic identity, version, imported packages and exported packages.",
      "Successful Java compilation does not prove that Apache Felix can resolve runtime package imports.",
      "A bundle, a Declarative Services component and a registered service are different runtime objects.",
      "A plain Java class inside a bundle is not automatically an OSGi component or service.",
      "@Component declares a Declarative Services component and @Reference expresses a service dependency.",
      "Required references and required configuration must be satisfied before a component can activate.",
      "A bundle can be Active while a contained component remains unsatisfied.",
      "The local AEM SDK exposes the Web Console; cloud environments expose read-only runtime evidence through Developer Console.",
      "A Resource exposes a path, name, resource type, properties and children without requiring direct JCR Node use.",
      "ValueMap supports typed property access and adaptTo bridges a Resource to supported higher-level abstractions.",
      "Prefer AEM product APIs, then Sling abstractions; use JCR only for JCR-specific needs and OSGi for container concerns.",
      "Administrative repository access is not allowed; background access uses a scoped service user and a correctly closed ResourceResolver.",
      "AEM as a Cloud Service treats deployed code and configuration as immutable at runtime."
    ],
    "canonical_terms": [
      "core",
      "OSGi bundle",
      "Apache Felix",
      "MANIFEST.MF",
      "Bundle-SymbolicName",
      "Import-Package",
      "Export-Package",
      "Declarative Services",
      "@Component",
      "@Reference",
      "service registry",
      "Installed",
      "Resolved",
      "Active",
      "unsatisfied",
      "Resource",
      "ValueMap",
      "ResourceResolver",
      "adaptTo"
    ]
  },
  "slide_local_context": {
    "required_background": "Show the preferred order AEM → Sling → JCR → OSGi. Examples: PageManager/Page; Resource/ValueMap; Session/Node for access control or JCR-specific needs; @Component/@Reference for container lifecycle. Add forbidden path: administrative resolver/session. Add safe background path: scoped service user → try-with-resources ResourceResolver → close."
  }
}

## Global Style
{
  "name": "technical atlas courseware",
  "visual_direction": "Sober, information-rich technical atlas blended with academic courseware. Use exact Maven modules, OSGi metadata, Declarative Services lifecycle states, resource-tree objects and diagnostic evidence instead of generic cloud or code illustrations.",
  "color_palette": "Warm ivory drafting-paper background, deep navy typography, faint square grid, cobalt blue for source and bundle traces, green for satisfied or active runtime behavior, violet for contracts and content abstractions, and restrained orange for unresolved or unsafe states.",
  "typography": "Large bold modern sans serif headings; crisp sans serif body copy; true monospace appearance for Java annotations, manifest headers, package names, paths, runtime states and API calls.",
  "texture_and_finish": "Flat 2D technical diagrams with fine rules and precise IDE, JAR, manifest, lifecycle, registry, resource-tree and console icons. No gradients, neon, glass, 3D or photography.",
  "deck_consistency": "Match the approved slide_04 sample palette, typography, drafting grid, technical density, semantic colors, monospace treatment and line weight while varying composition by slide role."
}

## Slide
{
  "number": 8,
  "title": "Choose the highest useful API.",
  "role": "decision ladder",
  "intent": "Avoid coupling ordinary component code to lower-level repository or container APIs."
}

## Text
{
  "title": "Choose the highest useful API.",
  "key_points": [
    "Prefer an AEM product abstraction when it directly models the requirement.",
    "Otherwise prefer Sling resources and requests.",
    "Use JCR only for JCR-specific capabilities.",
    "Use OSGi for container concerns.",
    "Background access uses a scoped service user and a correctly closed ResourceResolver."
  ],
  "speaker_focus": null
}

## Layout
{
  "composition": "Descending four-level decision ladder with examples, plus safe-versus-forbidden resolver access strip.",
  "intent": "Turn API preference into a practical choice rather than a hierarchy to memorize."
}

## Visual Elements
{
  "main_visual": "AEM-to-OSGi decision ladder and resolver ownership strip."
}

## Constraints
[
  "Render the order AEM → Sling → JCR → OSGi exactly.",
  "Do not imply JCR or OSGi APIs are universally forbidden.",
  "Explicitly mark administrative access as forbidden."
]

## Universal Constraints
- The final image itself must contain the title and key points.
- Render Chinese text exactly and legibly; avoid garbled characters.
- Keep the confirmed deck style consistent while varying layout by slide role.
- No watermark, unrelated logo, or extra slide number.
